data.frustration: Keeping up with changing regulations and laws regarding herbalism and supplements
data.why: This frustration affects a large audience of holistic health coaches, and the ever-changing regulatory landscape creates a huge need for infoproducts that can provide guidance and support

data.frustration: Lack of understanding and respect for herbalism from conventional healthcare professionals
data.why: Large audience of holistic health coaches are interested in herbalism and want to see it integrated into mainstream healthcare, but this frustration indicates a large potential market for infoproducts that can help bridge the gap

data.frustration: Difficulty in finding high-quality, sustainable, and eco-friendly herbal suppliers
data.why: While this frustration is real for some holistic health coaches, the audience is relatively niche, but the potential for infoproducts that can help solve this problem is still significant

data.frustration: Lack of standardization and consistency in herbal product quality
data.why: This frustration affects a moderate-sized audience of holistic health coaches, and the potential for infoproducts that can help solve this problem is significant, but not as large as some of the other frustrations

data.frustration: Creating and pricing herbal formulas that are effective yet affordable for clients
data.why: While this frustration is real for some holistic health coaches, the audience is relatively small, and the potential for infoproducts that can help solve this problem is moderate

data.frustration: Dealing with client skepticism and misinformation about herbalism
data.why: This frustration affects a relatively small audience of holistic health coaches, and while there is a need for infoproducts that can provide education and support, the potential market is limited

data.frustration: Finding the time and resources to develop and market their own herbal products
data.why: This frustration affects a small audience of holistic health coaches who want to create their own herbal products, but the potential market for infoproducts that can help solve this problem is limited

data.frustration: Dealing with competition from large herbal companies and online retailers
